---
title: "Move Semantics Explained"
---

# Move Semantics Explained
When a heap-backed value is assigned to another binding, passed to a function, or returned from a function, ownership is **moved**.

```rust
fn main() {
    let s1 = String::from("orders");
    let s2 = s1; // s1 is MOVED to s2

    // println!("{}", s1); // COMPILE ERROR: value borrowed here after move
    println!("s2 owns the heap buffer: {}", s2);
}
```

### Why Rust Moves Instead of Shallow Copying

If `s1` and `s2` both owned the same heap pointer, when both went out of scope, they would attempt to free the same memory twice—a catastrophic **double free** bug. Rust prevents this by invalidating `s1` at compile time with zero runtime cost.
